questions.question: What is a dependency in Dependency Injection?
options: A bug that stops the build
Any object a class needs to do its work
A Maven library that must be downloaded
A class that has no constructor
questions.explanation: A dependency is something a class needs, such as a payment gateway; DI hands it in from outside.

questions.question: Which injection style does Spring recommend for required dependencies?
options: Field injection
Static injection
Constructor injection
Reflection injection
questions.explanation: Constructor injection allows final fields, works without Spring in tests and fails early if something is missing.

questions.question: DeliveryService has a constructor taking PaymentGateway. In a test you write new DeliveryService(amount -> "Fake pay Rs " + amount) and call placeOrder("Biryani", 450), which returns dish + ": " + gateway.pay(amount). What is printed?
options: Biryani: Paid Rs 450 by UPI
Biryani: Fake pay Rs 450
Fake pay Rs 450: Biryani
A NullPointerException
questions.explanation: The fake gateway you passed in is used, so the fake text appears after the dish name.

questions.question: A service has a field private final PaymentGateway gateway = new UpiGateway(); and Spring is used to run the app. What is the problem?
options: Spring cannot start the app
The service builds its own helper, so it cannot be swapped or faked
final fields are not allowed in beans
UpiGateway must be an abstract class
questions.explanation: Using new inside the class is not injection; the service is tied to UpiGateway and hard to test.

questions.question: Two classes, UpiGateway and CardGateway, both implement PaymentGateway and both carry @Component. DeliveryService asks for a PaymentGateway. What happens at startup?
options: Spring picks the first class alphabetically
Spring injects both into one field
Startup fails because more than one bean matches
Spring creates a third bean automatically
questions.explanation: With two matching beans and no @Primary or @Qualifier, Spring cannot choose and reports an ambiguity error.
